title: Four-Dimensional CT Analysis Using Sequential 3D-3D Registration
protocol: Set up the CT machine.
Acquire CT examinations with a 320-detector-row CT system for multiple phases of 3D volume data with 160 mm craniocaudal coverage.
Rehearse joint movements from start position to end position before the exam.
Ask the subject to move the joint during the scan time and obtain series of volume data.
Store sequential volume data in DICOM format.
Perform static 3DCT of all target bones and store data in DICOM format.
Perform semiautomatic segmentation of 3DCT data.
Load CT DICOM data by selecting all DICOM files of the static 3DCT data.
Open the label field by clicking Edit New Label Field.
Check which threshold CT attenuation value is appropriate to extract cortical bone from the source bone.
Select materials with CT attenuation values above the threshold.
Manually modify the demarcation using an editing tool for consistency with the shape of the bone.
Generate the surface data (triangle meshes) from the labeled bone cortex position data (point cloud in the software).
Store the surface data by exporting data in Standard Triangulated Language (STL) format.
Click Generate Surface|Apply on the label of the cortical bone.
Click File|Export Data As|STL Binary Little Endian to save the surface data in STL format.
Perform automatic segmentation of 4DCT volume data.
Set the threshold of the bone cortex as in static CT.
Extract geometric data showing CT attenuation values above the threshold from all 51 frames of the 4DCT data using the DICOM reading module.
Adjust the threshold according to the bone density of the source bone.
Translate positional data into a format that can be interpreted by image processing software (e.g., Avizo).
Reconstruct all surface data of the point cloud with higher CT attenuation values than the threshold for all 4DCT frames using a batch processing script.
Perform surface registration from static 3DCT to the first frame of the 4DCT.
Trim bones in a static 3DCT into partial segment data included in all frames of 4DCT.
Use the Selecting Face function in 3D mesh editing software for ICP algorithm.
Pick three easily identifiable landmarks on fixed and moving bones using PickPoints function.
Match roughly the partial fixed and moving bones according to picked landmarks on the first frame of 4DCT surface data.
Perform surface registration using the ICP algorithm with open source software (e.g., VTK).
Calculate transformation matrices from static 3DCT to the first frame of 4DCT for both fixed and moving bones.
Derive a transformation matrix causing reverse action if necessary.
Perform sequential surface registration.
Match the partial surfaces of the fixed and moving bone in the first 4DCT frame onto the surface data of the second frame.
Match the partial surfaces of the ith frame onto the (i + 1)th frame of 4DCT sequentially.
Repeat this process until the last frame of the 4DCT using the ICP module in open source software.
Calculate transformation matrices from the static 3DCT to all frames in 4DCT based on the results obtained.
Reconstruct moving bone motion with respect to the fixed bone.
Define coordinate systems for the fixed and moving bones when rotation parameters are measured.
